The restoration of one of Braddon's oldest buildings will begin in a matter of weeks, the developers planning to build a 14-storey apartment building behind it have confirmed.

Login or signup to continue reading

The revamping of the Coggan's Bakery building is part of the Roland Development Group's plan to build a two-building mixed-use apartment complex on the corner of Mort Street and Elouera Street.

The confirmation that work would soon begin on the site came as the developer submitted a number of amendments to its development application for the project which would reduce the bulk of the proposed buildings and give more prominence to the Coggan's Bakery building.

Coggan's Bakery operated on Mort Street from 1925 to 1991. In 2011, the building was given heritage protection for its "special association with the early planning and design of Canberra", but has since been damaged by vandals and covered in graffiti.

In 2024, Roland Development Group purchased the site, along with the neighbouring car wash, with the intention of creating a "vibrant" mixed-use development across the two blocks. The first plans for the project were put before the planning authority in December 2025.

Those plans include a 14-storey, 129-apartment building, which would be built slightly set back around the Coggan's Bakery building, while a 12-storey mixed-use development with hotel rooms, commercial units and another 64 apartments would be built on the car wash site.

Last week, Roland Development Group submitted a number of refinements to the development application in response to feedback from both government agencies and the public, Chris Roland said.

"We have received a lot of positive feedback about the restoration of Coggan's Bakery, the public spaces we're creating, the laneways, the mix of residential and commercial uses and the potential to bring a hotel and supermarket to the heart of Braddon," Mr Roland said.

Much of the concern surrounding the original application centred on the height of the two buildings.
